chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: The country club party, tips and giving away half-pints in a cab
summary: At Bales's country club party he made big tips plus a $20 check and a basket of half-pints, and handed them out from a cab on 18th and 12th Streets.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, all I was doing, making during that time, let's see, I think about $2 a night or something like that, you know, because I had left the Monroe Inn--
It sounds dreadful, but you could sort of live reasonably on that in those days.

Yes. You wasn't making no money, but what little money that you had, it went a long ways, you know. And that was the thing about it, you know. And so I went out and played this party for him and -- at this country club -- and so people was tipping me and so, "Play so on and so on," give me a dollar, dollar. I had my pockets full, you know. So when I got through playing, you know, the guy says, "Look here. Would you like to -- say, I've got a whole basket of these half-pints over here. There's nothing wrong with them,

but these guys just bought them and just poured a drink off and just left them here. Would you want to take some of this stuff with you?" I said, "Yeah," so he gave me almost a bushel basket full of stuff like that. Booze, you know.
And so I started out the door. He says, "Wait a minute. I haven't paid you yet." I said, "Oh, I forgot. See, I made these tips." I forgot about it, you know what I mean.
He said, "What do I owe you?" I said, "Oh, I don't know. Whatever you want to give me." And so he gave me a check for $20 and I like to fell out. "Oh, a check for $20 --"
Was that Mr. Bales that did that?
No, this was the fella at the country club. But Mr. Bales was the one that got me the job. And he wrote me a check for $20. "Is that all right?" I said, "Fine, well, yes." You know?

And so, I called me a cab and I came on in town. And I got -- I'm sitting in the back of the cab, all this booze. I go up and down 18th and 12th Streets -- you know, that's 12th & Vine, 18th & Vine. All that stuff.
I go up and down that row. "Come in." "Hey," cab come up there. "Give him a half pint." "Okay, go
ahead, driver." Next came up. "Hold it, driver."
Driving through the streets, giving away half-pints. And you know, I was happy, felt good, you know. And I kept a pretty good portion for myself, you know, took the rest home and so --
These were people you knew, were they, that you were giving them out --
